title: UI Cookbook & Migration Guide for Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a single authoritative "UI Cookbook" section on the design docs site that consolidates usage guidance, concrete examples, do/don'ts, API surface notes, and migration steps for the core design primitives we maintain (tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts). Deliverables: 1) Token usage guide and token map + migration mapping from legacy token names, 2) Button API docs with prop examples and accessible patterns, 3) Table patterns (virtualization, pagination, row/column API), 4) Chart color and annotation guidance tied to tokens, 5) Migration playbook including codemods, deprecation timeline, and comms templates. Scope: Focus on surface-level developer-facing docs (component props, examples, code snippets, migration steps). Defer deep engineering implementation (runtime changes, build tooling) to ENG tickets: will reference ENG work and PRs. Success criteria: - Single-page entry for each primitive with examples in React + HTML snippets - Migration checklist that reduces manual migration time by ~60% (est) - Signoff from engineering and platform docs owner - Publish to docs site and announce on internal channels
comments: 2025-11-12 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff. Draft outline created. Decided to treat tokens and components as separate micro-sections to keep pages scannable. Will prototype buttons first as they have the highest consumer churn.

2025-11-18 — Marcus Lee: Engineering alignment meeting notes: ENG to provide codemod for legacy token name -> new token var mapping. ENG will expose Button props mapping in the next PR (ref: GH-PR-1123). We agreed on prop names: variant, size, tone, disabled, loading, as string-literal props rather than boolean-heavy API.

2025-11-22 — Design review: Draft Button examples ready in Figma (link below). PM requested explicit `danger` usage guidance and suggested a 'do/don't' side-by-side example for CTA vs destructive actions.

2025-11-28 — Accessibility review by Jordan Kim: Buttons need clear focus ring examples for high-contrast mode. Tables should include keyboard navigation and ARIA examples. Added a short checklist to the Table page for keyboard/announce behaviors.

2025-12-01 — Marcus Lee: Added migration steps for tokens. Created initial codemod in GH (GH-PR-1148). Noted caveat: color tokens that were runtime-overridden in some apps will need manual verification; codemod will flag these files for review.
2025-12-02 — Aisha Patel: Incorporated engineering feedback and consolidated examples. Ready for cross-team review. Requested verification from DataViz team on chart color semantics.

2025-12-03 — Design critique: Minor wording tweaks requested (avoid 'primary' as a tone label, prefer 'accent' in docs). Planning a staged publish: internal preview -> 1-week feedback window -> public docs release.
notes: Key decisions and trade-offs: 1) Token naming mapping will be opinionated and we will keep a two-release deprecation window for legacy names; 2) Button API favors explicit string variants to align with platform SDKs and reduce runtime branching; 3) Tables docs will recommend virtualization for >500 rows but provide fallback code for simpler paginated tables; 4) Charts guidance will centralize color palettes on tokens to avoid visual drift across apps. Migration plan highlights: - Phase 1 (docs + codemods): publish migration guide and codemod; educate maintainers. - Phase 2 (deprecation): mark legacy CSS vars/classes deprecated, add console warnings in DEV builds. - Phase 3 (removal): remove legacy aliases after 2 releases and communicate to integrators.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Docs pages published with React and plain-HTML examples for Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts; 2) Two sample migration runs completed by ENG on internal apps and results documented; 3) Accessibility checklist items verified by accessibility engineer; 4) At least one consumer team (Editor, Dashboard) signs off on examples and migration steps.
open_questions: Should we provide automated visual-regression tests tied to examples in docs or leave that to consumer teams?
What exact deprecation messaging cadence is required by Product for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private deployments?
Do we standardize on 'accent' vs 'primary' for token naming across all component docs?
